::: {#def-fdr}
#### False discovery rate

For a family of tests with $V$ false positives among $R$ rejections (@def-rejection-counts),
the **false discovery proportion** (FDP) is the fraction of rejections that are false positives,
counted as 0 when there are no rejections,
and the **false discovery rate** (FDR) is its expected value:

$$
\text{FDP} \eqdef \frac{V}{\max(R, 1)},
\qquad
\text{FDR} \eqdef \E{\text{FDP}}.
$$

A procedure **controls the FDR at level $q$** if $\text{FDR} \le q$
for every possible set of true null hypotheses.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
#### Source

The false discovery rate was introduced by Benjamini and Hochberg [-@benjamini1995controlling];
the notation $V$, $S$, $U$, $T$ and $R$ follows @james2021islr2e [ch. 13].
:::
